blockingFindings.summary: The installed runtime has a proposal/state-output surface but no public uninstall facts builder, proposal-digest binding, or installed detached removal entrypoint that performs and verifies filesystem removal.

cases.area: Japanese register, mixed technical language, encoded input, Unicode, and paths
cases.limitation: Deterministic classification is not general semantic understanding.
cases.observation: 14 corpus entries preserved authority and expected outcomes

cases.area: Japanese high-risk, absurd, Unknown, and human-confirmation STOP boundary
cases.limitation: The policy boundary does not authenticate the human or execute provider controls.
cases.observation: Every corpus high-risk operation requires human_confirmation_required

cases.area: Executable Wizard and CLI Japanese interaction
cases.limitation: Resource parity alone cannot prove executable Japanese interaction.
cases.observation: Both Wizard entrypoints consume the strict Japanese resource layer with executable tests

cases.limitation: A Japanese guide to an English Status is not output parity.
cases.observation: Japanese Status view is derived from the same machine facts

cases.area: Task Outcome PR summary Japanese parity
cases.limitation: PR localization must not translate or invent arbitrary evidence prose.
cases.observation: Japanese PR chrome preserves the approved field set

cases.limitation: Arbitrary evidence prose remains source text and is not machine-translated.
cases.observation: Japanese Task Outcome chrome is derived from unchanged machine facts

cases.area: Executable Japanese adopter lifecycle through uninstall proposal and model boundary
cases.limitation: The fixture proves bounded repository behavior and Japanese evidence handling; it does not prove filesystem removal, general fluency, provider operations, or real adopter platform quality.
cases.observation: Isolated Japanese adopter fixture executes installation, calibration, recovery, uninstall proposal, and detached-removal model boundaries

cases.area: Japanese installation, calibration, upgrade, rollback, uninstall, and recovery path
cases.limitation: Structure and terminology checks do not replace native technical editing.
cases.observation: All required Japanese documents and an actionable uninstall path are present

cases.limitation: A proposal or in-memory model is not filesystem-removal evidence; provider permissions and platform locks remain adopter responsibilities.
cases.observation: The installed runtime has a proposal/state-output surface but no public uninstall facts builder, proposal-digest binding, or installed detached removal entrypoint that performs and verifies filesystem removal.

cases.area: Japanese document metadata and three-language structure
cases.limitation: Automated parity checks cannot establish complete translation quality.
cases.observation: Required Japanese engineer entry documents exist and remain under metadata checks

cases.limitation: Passing the gate proves only the in-repository matrix at the assessed source.
cases.observation: check-release-preflight requires the current Japanese assessment

cases.area: General Japanese model fluency and human translation quality
cases.limitation: General Japanese provider/model fluency and human translation quality remain unproved.
cases.observation: No provider-backed or native-human-reviewed general fluency evidence is claimed.

limitations: This assessment does not claim general model fluency, translation quality, or provider behavior.
Every English-inferred, missing, stale, or non-executable Japanese capability is release-blocking.
